A close reading for the week

“Unsex me here”

Macbeth · Act 1, Scene 5

Lady Macbeth has just heard that Duncan will sleep beneath her roof. What follows is a series of appeals: to spirits, to her body, to night and to concealment. She is asking for a cruelty she does not yet trust herself to have.

The raven himself is hoarse
That croaks the fatal entrance of Duncan
Under my battlements. Come, you spirits
That tend on mortal thoughts,1 unsex me here,2

  1. 1

    Death enters the thought

    “Mortal” can mean human, but here it also carries the force of death-dealing. Lady Macbeth asks for more than numbness. She summons agents associated with the murderous thought she wants to complete.

  2. 2

    Unsexing

    The command asks for sexed identity and bodily association to be stripped away or remade. The rest of the speech specifies what she rejects: milk, remorse and the “visitings” of a nature she believes may interrupt her purpose.
